newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Bangladesh water-sharing talks deadlocked.
newsitem.headline: India, Bangladesh water-sharing talks deadlocked.

text.p: Talks between India and Bangladesh over sharing water from the River Ganges ended in stalemate here on Tuesday, officials said.
The talks were held between the communist chief minister of West Bengal state, Jyoti Basu, and Bangladesh's foreign minister Abdus Samad Azad.
Basu said the issue has now been referred to a special committee which includes officials from both countries.
"We are not in a position to release the quantum of water they are asking for. The arithmetic calculations are not tallying," he said after the talks.
Nevertheless Azad described the meeting as "fruitful" and said the talks were held in a cordial atmosphere.
"Our demand was a permament solution to the long-standing problem and we have apprised Basu of our view," he said.

Sharing of water from the Ganges has been a major irritant in relations between Dhaka and Delhi since India commissioned its Farakka barrage, 18 km (12 miles) from Bangladesh's northern border, in 1974.
Officials claim more than 40 million people in northwestern Bangladesh have faced gradual desertification because of the control of the flow of the Ganges.
The last agreement on sharing the Ganges expired in 1988, and attempts to renew it since then have failed.
The Ganges flows into Bangladesh through West Bengal.
